scope: Scalar fused gate/up projections on the mixed-format Q4 target. The existing two-row kernel now specializes each weight format independently; no floating-point operation/order, weights, sampler, controller or batched verification changes.
retained: Four format pairs: Q4_K/Q5_K, Q4_K/IQ4_XS, IQ4_XS/Q4_K and IQ4_XS/Q5_K. Existing same-format specializations and generic fallback remain. No runtime options.

One consolidated fused-versus-verification test replaces the older same-format-only helper; existing independent decode controls remain. The maintained geometry tool accepts an optional scalar up-format.

actual_weight_confirmation.method: Actual mixed-format target gate/up pairs, read-only whole GGUF registration. Existing runtime-format fused kernel versus the same arithmetic specialized independently for gate/up formats. Six alternating-order rounds, six rotations of all matching pairs; outputs finite and bit-identical.

fused_contract.note: One shared fused-versus-verification test replaces the older same-format-only function. Two distinct inputs, finite bitwise comparisons, mixed formats, partial row groups, and the full-size Q8/Q6 controls.

q8_scope.reason: No Q8-target FFN tensor pair selects any new specialization, including auxiliary tensors. Full-size Q8 and Q6 fused operators pass the consolidated suite; prior Q8 target qualification remains in dflash2-width2.json.

quality.other_drafts: Q8/BF16 draft code is unchanged; preceding qualification is linked from dflash2-width2.json. No new full-model run for those drafts.

speed.method: Q4 target, C1. AR pp2048/tg128 at depth0, one timed repetition per invocation after the built-in32-token warmup, two samples per binary in ABBA order. Separate Q4 draft DFlash2 raw JSON/prose TG300 controls, one baseline/candidate pair per workload; includes prefill, excludes model loading. Compare each continuation against existing qualified AR IDs. AR prefill and generation are separate benchmark phases; depth-zero generation has the benchmark 16-token seed, not a 2048-token prefix.
speed.limits: Bounded probe: two AR samples per binary, one DFlash2 sample per binary/workload. AR prefill mean changes -0.71%; first baseline is 425.70 and the other three rows are 420.15-420.78 tok/s. The scalar specialization does not affect prefill kernels; no prefill improvement is claimed. DFlash2 controls are flat within noise.

profile.method: Separate baseline/candidate Nix release AR repetition TG128 profiles. Compare the old runtime-format fused kernel with the candidate union of its remaining runtime-format calls and four new mixed-format variants; unchanged mixed formats remain in both unions. Call counts match, and all four new variants have zero private scratch. Trace timings are diagnostic; use the unprofiled benchmark for throughput.

profile_limits: The selected union contains 27 FFNs per AR token: 17 new mixed specializations and 10 unchanged runtime-format calls. Its 3.56% time reduction is not isolated timing of the 17 affected FFNs. The four specialized kernels have VGPR64 and zero scratch; the remaining generic kernel still has scratch8.

rejected_experiments.method: Scalar launch dispatcher versus staged exact FP32 kernels, actual target GGUF, read-only whole-file registration. Six rotated-order rounds, six rotations each, up to16 same-shape tensors or one1GB head; all outputs checked finite and bit-identical.
rejected_experiments.decision: Standalone Q4 up/down improve 9.6/8.8%, but AR gate/up are fused and only five target down FFNs are Q4. Not integrated; other formats flat or slower.

rejected_experiments.method: Actual same-format target gate/up pairs, read-only whole GGUF registration. Exact scalar fused SwiGLU versus staged interleaved gate/up rows, same FP32 operation order and expf epilogue. Six rotated-order rounds, six rotations of up to16 pairs; all outputs finite and bit-identical.
rejected_experiments.decision: Q4 same-format improves 4.9% in isolation but covers only three FFN pairs; not retained because it adds a separate kernel for a small total opportunity. Q5 flat, IQ4 slower.

rejected_experiments.method: Actual Q5 GGUF projections at total verification batch8, whole-file read-only registration. Qualified all-eight-token kernel versus two/four independently scheduled token groups, using existing TokenGroups templates and preserving each dot/reduction order. Six rotated-order rounds with six rotations of up to16 same-shape tensors; all outputs finite and bit-identical.
rejected_experiments.decision: Splitting total batch8 into two/four groups preserves exact outputs but reduces throughput by 22-50% on all three Q5 projection shapes. No production change. This duplicates weight decoding/staging; no cache-counter attribution is claimed.

limits: Quality is retained against qualified Gufo AR and existing upstream draft references; this is not independent original-target/checkpoint proof.
No new full depth matrix, C>1 or capability result. The prior speculative table remains the better-sampled dflash2-width2.json measurement.
The upstream performance goal remains open. Artifact, power and timing differences are documented in llama-comparison.json.

follow_up_probes.source_review: Pinned ROCMFPX-NOTES.md was re-read through remote gh; its SHA256 matches the existing llama-comparison.json audit. Whole-block scale amortization and hoisting decode out of the token loop already exist in Gufo verification. The following probes test additional exact transformations.

experiments.reason: Wave-uniform row indexing is flat on Q5 up and slower on down/medium; explicit two-superblock scalar d/dmin header loads are 8.8-15.0% slower. Register reductions do not produce a throughput win.
experiments.method: Actual Q5 GGUF batch8 projections. Whole-file read-only registration; six rotated-order rounds x six rotations of up to16 same-shape tensors. Baseline versus explicit wave-uniform row indexing and a second variant with uniform two-superblock d/dmin header loads. Every output finite and bit-identical.

experiments.reason: Expanding Q5 integer codes from176 to272bytes per block preserves every coefficient but adds54.55% weight bytes. Even with unsigned-byte conversions it reduces throughput22.6-31.2%; the signed-pointer control is slower still. An identical-byte copy control distinguishes packing from mapping differences. Packing/loading time is excluded, so this is already favorable to expansion.
experiments.method: Actual Q5 GGUF batch8, original read-only mapping versus identical-byte anonymous copy versus expanded 272-byte blocks (original16-byte scales/header +256exact integer codes). All are read-only registered. Six rotated-order rounds x six rotations of up to8 same-shape tensors, all outputs finite/bit-identical. Copy/unpack time excluded; expanded weight bytes are 54.5% greater, printed per variant. Unsigned-code variant exposes the known0..31 range to the compiler; signed-code control retains the baseline pointer type. No production format or path is changed.

experiments.reason: Keeping Q6 codes0..63 until unsigned float conversion, then subtracting32 exactly, preserves all outputs. Batch4 is flat (-0.20%) and batch8 loses8.16%. No format, geometry or output arithmetic changes are retained.
experiments.method: Actual1GB Q6 vocabulary head, batch4/8, whole-GGUF read-only registration. Same retained W16/R3/T2 geometry and FP32 sums. Candidate keeps decoded codes0..63, converts unsigned bytes then subtracts32 exactly in float, avoiding packed signed-byte subtraction. Six alternating-order rounds, six launches each; every output finite/bit-identical before timing. No production changes.
